title: Extract simulated client layer and harden regression pipeline
creator: Amelia Chen
description:
Background: Our regression and load harness has accreted multiple behavior models (synthetic sequencers, prefix-caching tests, and a small simulated client harness) that are duplicated across eval pipelines and CI jobs. This duplication makes incremental changes risky, increases test fragility, and forces repeated dependency upgrades across several repositories.

Scope: Extract a single, lightweight 'simulated client' library from the regression harness into sources/perf-client package, implement a stable adapter interface for new and legacy load plugins, and harden the regression pipeline with clearer staging, retries, and artifact provenance. This ticket covers code extraction, interface definition, CI job changes, dependency upgrades required by the new package, and a rollout plan to migrate two key regression suites to the new client.

Goals: 
- Reduce duplicated simulated-client code across 3 repos to a single package.
- Introduce a plugin adapter boundary that isolates load-driver implementations from harness orchestration.
- Upgrade core runtime test deps (aiohttp -> 3.9.x to 4.0.x, grpcio 1.56 -> 1.58) and pin binary wheels in CI to avoid ABI breaks.
- Improve regression pipeline resilience: explicit seeding, deterministic variation control, and clearer pass/fail signal mapping to telemetry.
- Keep rolling-window latency regression tests stable under autoscaling by adding warmup and KV-cache priming steps.

Non-goals: Full rewrite of the primary load generator; replacing existing scenario DSL. Migration of every integration test in this sprint is out of scope.

Acceptance Criteria: 
- A new package sources/perf-client with documented adapter interface, unit tests, and CI publish job (nightly wheel build).
- Two existing regression suites (reg-suite-tokenization and reg-suite-chatstream) migrated to the new client and green in CI for three consecutive runs.
- Dependency upgrade matrix documented and pinned in CI to avoid unexpected wheel rebuilds.
- Dashboard (perf-regressions) shows stable signal after migration with run metadata including client package version and seed.
- Rollback plan documented and tested: ability to run legacy harness for a single CI job if an issue is detected.

Risks & Trade-offs: 
- Upgrading grpcio/aiohttp may hit binary wheel incompatibilities on our self-hosted runners; mitigation is to pin wheels and add a canary runner using new wheels.
- Consolidation centralizes risk: a bug in perf-client could affect multiple suites; we mitigate via strong unit tests and a staged rollout.
- Short-term increased CI runtime while adding warmup/priming steps; accepted for long-term signal quality.

Deliverables: 
- GH PR: redwood/perf-client: extract simulated-client and adapter boundary. 
- CI changes: move reg-suite jobs to use perf-client wheel and add a nightly wheel-publish workflow.
- Docs: README for adapter interface, migration guide, and failure rollback runbook.

Metrics for success: 
- Reduction in duplicated files by at least 60% across reg suites.
- Flakiness rate for migrated suites decreases by 30% (measured by rerun frequency).
- No customer-facing incidents attributable to harness after migration.
